summary: Pier light at the west entrance pier of Sodus Bay, Lake Ontario: a 1938 tower and a 4th-order lens moved from the 1871 shore house in 1901; Coast Guard owned, pier open.

lens.note: Moved from the 1871 shore lighthouse to the outer pier tower on 10 June 1901 (LighthouseFriends; Board 1901 report records the order change).

light.note: Pier light. The shore lighthouse at Sodus Point was first built in 1825 (Society).

events.note: Shore lighthouse at Sodus Bay (the 1825 tower), demolished 1871.
Stone tower on the west pier, described by LighthouseFriends.
Pier light first shown from the 1837 tower (LighthouseFriends).
Gale destroyed the pier beacon.
Pair of range lights on masts replaced the pier beacon.
Congress funded a new dwelling and tower for $14,000 (July 1870).
New limestone shore lighthouse completed 30 June 1871; old tower of 1825 demolished.
Frame towers replaced the range masts; 1,150-foot elevated walk built on the pier.
In the fiscal year ended 30 June 1892 (Board report, scan p. 523): vessel of Windsor, Ontario, sheered into and broke down some 10 feet of the elevated walk while being towed outward.
Inner beacon on the west pier moved about 25 feet to a new tower, 6 July 1895.
New beacon with lantern built to replace an unserviceable one; keeper's dwelling extensively repaired. The 1896 Board report calls this the previous year.
Outer light changed from sixth to fourth order, 10 June 1901.
Fourth-order lens taken from the shore lighthouse and transferred to the outer pier tower.
Shore lighthouse discontinued; keeper stayed on to tend the pier lights.
Air fog signal established at the end of the pier, 3 June 1926.
Assistant keeper Charles A. Plummer recognised for rescuing a boy and girl whose canoe overturned near the lighthouse.
Wooden outer tower replaced by the present square pyramidal tower; light converted from kerosene to electricity.
Coast Guard watch (Thomas M. Muchow) rescued a man who had fallen off the breakwall into the channel, 31 August 1964.
Coast Guard closed its station at Sodus Point; a commander kept living in the lighthouse.
LighthouseFriends dates the National Register listing to 1976. The Society dates it to 1977.
Shore lighthouse transferred to the Town of Sodus after a period of vandalism and neglect.
Sodus Bay Historical Society museum opened in the shore lighthouse, 4 July 1985.
Fresnel lens returned to the tower (Society).

corrections.why: The pier light had a stone tower on the west pier from 1837 (LighthouseFriends). The 1901 date is when the outer light was changed to a fourth-order lens (Board report 1901). The shore light was built in 1825 (Society).
The present tower has a focal plane of 51 feet (LighthouseFriends), about 15.5 m. The record's 5.5 m is not supported by any source read here.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives the tower as built in 1858 (Wikidata) and first lit in 1901 (Rowlett). LighthouseFriends describes an 1837 stone pier tower, the 1857 gale, 1858 range lights on masts, 1872 frame towers, and the 1938 present tower. The Society dates the shore lighthouse to 1871. The 1858 date belongs to the range lights in LighthouseFriends' account, not to a tower standing today.
LighthouseFriends dates the National Register listing to 1976; the Society dates it to 1977. Unresolved; the story gives both.
The USLHS roster is one list for the Sodus Point station. It covers both the shore light and the pier lights, and it does not separate them; the story says so.

notes_for_editor: (1) The archive's 'Sodus Point (Old)' roster is the only keeper list found and it covers the shore light and the pier lights together; LighthouseFriends says the keeper was responsible solely for the pier lights after 1901, but the roster does not separate the stints. A human should check whether the roster lines before about 1901 belong to the shore light only. (2) The 1857 gale, the 1858 range lights and the 1871 construction come from LighthouseFriends and the Society, not from the Board's reports, which are not in the local corpus for those years. The Board's FY1892, FY1896 and FY1901 entries are primary and checked (the Windsor entry is scan p. 523, inside the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1892, not 1891). (3) The record's characteristic (Fl G 4s, ENC) differs from Wikipedia's Isophase White 6s, which cites the Coast Guard Light List; Wikipedia was not used and the Light List was not read. Check before publishing the light's characteristic. (4) The Coast Guard Historian's Sodus Outer Lighthouse article (history.uscg.mil article 1989208) appeared in a search result saying the wooden tower was built in 1858 and replaced in 1938; the archived copy could not be read (binary response), so it is not cited. (5) us-lighthouses.com (search snippet only) says the outer light was automated in 1984; not verified, not used. (6) Newspaper searches (Chronicling America) found nothing on the 1857 gale, Daniel Phillips, or the 1935 rescue. (7) The 1964 rescue and the 1985 dedication details are from LighthouseFriends only. The story names only Thomas M. Muchow (a 1964 rescue, printed by LighthouseFriends) and no living private individuals. The 1985 dedication remark about the keeper's family is paraphrased without names. (8) The 1891 vessel's name is an OCR problem ('LaurOy'); the story does not name the vessel. (9) Museum hours are from the Society's website and may be out of date. (10) The keeper Charles A. Plummer appears on the roster as first assistant with 'at least' dates; the 1935 rescue is LighthouseFriends' statement. (11) Name variant: LighthouseFriends prints 'Grant R. Genter'; the roster says 'Grant C. Genter'. (12) Photos: none added.
